name: SIGMA - Cron Configuration File Created or Modified
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects auditd PATH records for writes to system crontabs, the cron.d / cron.* drop-in
directories, or per-user crontabs in /var/spool/cron. Cron executes whatever is written
there on a schedule (as root for system crontabs), giving execution, persistence and
potentially privilege escalation. The PARENT path record (the directory entry auditd
logs alongside the file) is filtered so each change raises one alert. Requires the
audit watch rules in docs/lab-integration.md (-w <path> -p wa -k cron_persistence).
false_positives: Package installation (e.g. logrotate, certbot) drops files in /etc/cron.d and cron.daily. Correlate with the SYSCALL record exe field (dpkg/apt) or change windows.
Users editing their own crontab with "crontab -e".
query: event.module:auditd AND ((file.path:(\/etc\/crontab* OR \/etc\/cron.d\/* OR \/etc\/cron.hourly\/* OR \/etc\/cron.daily\/* OR \/etc\/cron.weekly\/* OR \/etc\/cron.monthly\/* OR \/var\/spool\/cron\/*)))

name: SIGMA - SSH authorized_keys File Modified
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects auditd PATH records showing a write to an authorized_keys or authorized_keys2
file. Adding a public key there grants password-less SSH access that survives password
resets, so it is a favoured persistence mechanism (and privilege escalation when the
file belongs to root). The PARENT path record is filtered to avoid duplicates. Requires
audit watches on the relevant .ssh directories (see docs/lab-integration.md).
false_positives: Users adding their own keys, configuration management (Ansible authorized_key module), cloud-init on first boot.
query: event.module:auditd AND ((file.path:(*\/.ssh\/authorized_keys OR *\/.ssh\/authorized_keys2)))

name: SIGMA - Setuid or Setgid Bit Set With chmod
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects chmod being used to set the setuid or setgid bit (symbolic u+s/g+s/+s or
numeric modes 4xxx/2xxx/6xxx). A setuid-root copy of a shell or interpreter lets any
later local user regain root, so attackers who briefly gain root use this as a privilege
escalation backdoor. Package managers set these bits legitimately during installs, so
chmod calls started by a package manager or by a package maintainer script
(/var/lib/dpkg/info/*.postinst, rpm scriptlets) are filtered.
false_positives: Administrators building custom tools that require setuid. These should be rare and change-managed.
query: (event.category:process AND event.type:start) AND ((process.executable:*\/chmod AND (process.command_line:(*\ u\+s\ * OR *\ g\+s\ * OR *\ \+s\ * OR *\ 4755\ * OR *\ 4777\ * OR *\ 4711\ * OR *\ 2755\ * OR *\ 6755\ *))) AND (NOT ((process.parent.executable:(*\/dpkg OR *\/rpm OR *\/apt OR *\/apt\-get OR *\/yum OR *\/dnf)) OR (process.parent.command_line:(*\/var\/lib\/dpkg\/info\/* OR *\/var\/tmp\/rpm\-tmp.*)))))

name: SIGMA - File Upload With curl or wget
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects curl or wget being used to send a local file to a remote server (curl -T /
--upload-file, curl form or data upload with "@file", wget --post-file / --body-file).
These are standard tools present on almost every Linux host, which makes them the
simplest way to exfiltrate collected data over plain HTTP(S) or FTP without bringing any
attacker tooling. Downloads (the common legitimate case) are not matched.
false_positives: CI/CD jobs and backup scripts that upload artefacts to internal repositories. Allow-list by destination host or service account.
API clients posting JSON from files during development.
query: (event.category:process AND event.type:start) AND ((process.executable:*\/curl AND (process.command_line:(*\ \-T\ * OR *\ \-\-upload\-file\ * OR *\=@* OR *\ \-d\ @* OR *\ \-\-data\ @* OR *\ \-\-data\-binary\ @*))) OR (process.executable:*\/wget AND (process.command_line:(*\-\-post\-file* OR *\-\-body\-file*))))

name: SIGMA - Reverse Shell Command Line Patterns
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan (adaptation); original SigmaHQ rule(s) by @d4ns4n_, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems); Florian Roth (Nextron Systems); frack113
description:
Detects command lines characteristic of interactive reverse shells on Linux - bash
redirection to /dev/tcp or /dev/udp, netcat started with -e/-c to execute a shell, the
mkfifo + "sh -i" + nc pipe, and the Python socket + pty.spawn one-liner. A reverse shell
is how an attacker turns a single command execution into an interactive session that
connects outwards (bypassing inbound firewalls). Health checks against localhost that
use /dev/tcp are filtered.
false_positives: Container health checks or scripts that probe remote ports with bash /dev/tcp. Extend the filter with the specific internal hosts once verified.
Penetration testing activity.
query: (event.category:process AND event.type:start) AND (((process.command_line:(*\/dev\/tcp\/* OR *\/dev\/udp\/*)) OR ((process.executable:(*\/nc OR *\/ncat OR *\/netcat OR *\/nc.traditional)) AND (process.command_line:(*\ \-e\ \/bin\/* OR *\ \-c\ \/bin\/* OR *\ \-e\ sh* OR *\ \-e\ bash*))) OR (process.command_line:*mkfifo* AND process.command_line:*sh\ \-i* AND process.command_line:*nc\ *) OR (process.command_line:*socket* AND process.command_line:*connect* AND process.command_line:*pty.spawn*)) AND (NOT (process.command_line:(*\/dev\/tcp\/127.0.0.1\/* OR *\/dev\/tcp\/localhost\/*))))

name: SIGMA - Read or Copy of /etc/shadow via Command Line Tools
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects common file-reading, copying, encoding or transfer utilities being run with
/etc/shadow or /etc/gshadow on the command line, plus execution of John the Ripper's
"unshadow" helper. /etc/shadow holds the password hashes of local accounts; reading it
(root required) is the Linux analogue of dumping the SAM and is followed by offline
cracking. Legitimate administration uses vipw/passwd/chage rather than cat or cp.
false_positives: Backup jobs that archive /etc with tar (they include /etc/shadow on the command line only if listed explicitly). Allow-list the backup service account.
Compliance scanners that inspect shadow file permissions with cat or head.
query: (event.category:process AND event.type:start) AND (((process.command_line:(*\/etc\/shadow* OR *\/etc\/gshadow*)) AND (process.executable:(*\/cat OR *\/less OR *\/more OR *\/head OR *\/tail OR *\/cp OR *\/scp OR *\/base64 OR *\/xxd OR *\/strings OR *\/tar OR *\/zip OR *\/curl OR *\/nc))) OR process.executable:*\/unshadow)

name: SIGMA - Web Server Process Spawning a Shell or Recon Tool
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan (adaptation); original SigmaHQ rule(s) by Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects a web server or PHP-FPM worker starting a shell, a reconnaissance command or a
download / networking utility. A web application should serve requests, not spawn
/bin/sh or whoami; when it does, the usual cause is a web shell that was dropped on the
server or a command-injection / RCE vulnerability being exploited. The child-process view
catches post-exploitation regardless of the specific exploit used.
false_positives: CGI applications and PHP code that legitimately call shell helpers (mail(), ImageMagick wrappers). Allow-list by the exact CommandLine after review.
Java application servers are intentionally not included as parents because they spawn shells routinely; see docs/rules.md.
query: (event.category:process AND event.type:start) AND (((process.parent.executable:(*\/httpd OR *\/apache2 OR *\/nginx OR *\/lighttpd OR *\/caddy)) OR process.parent.executable:*\/php\-fpm*) AND (process.executable:(*\/sh OR *\/bash OR *\/dash OR *\/zsh OR *\/whoami OR *\/id OR *\/uname OR *\/nc OR *\/ncat OR *\/curl OR *\/wget OR *\/python3 OR *\/perl)))

name: SIGMA - DNS Query With Unusually Long Subdomain Label (Possible Tunneling)
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects DNS queries (Zeek dns.log) whose left-most label is 40 or more characters of
Base32/Base64/hex-like text. DNS tunneling tools (iodine, dnscat2, DNSExfiltrator) encode
data into subdomains of an attacker-controlled zone, so exfiltrated data appears as long,
high-entropy labels (the protocol limit is 63 characters per label). Normal hostnames are
short and dictionary-like. Known security vendors that use long hashed labels for
reputation lookups are filtered. The filter is a deliberate noise-versus-coverage trade-off:
every excluded zone is a blind spot, e.g. tunneling through an attacker-controlled name
under amazonaws.com (e.g. an S3 bucket or API Gateway endpoint) would not alert.
false_positives: Security products and CDNs that encode hashes in DNS labels (extend the filter with the specific zones seen in the environment).
DKIM / DMARC-related TXT lookups can have long selectors.
query: event.dataset:zeek.dns AND (dns.question.name:/.*[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,}\..*/ AND (NOT (dns.question.name:(*.sophosxl.net OR *.avts.mcafee.com OR *.amazonaws.com))))

name: SIGMA - Web Exploitation Patterns in HTTP Request URI
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects HTTP requests (Zeek http.log) whose URI contains classic exploitation payloads -
directory traversal (plain and URL-encoded), requests for /etc/passwd, SQL injection
"UNION SELECT", reflected script tags, Log4Shell JNDI lookups and command injection
into a shell. This is network-side evidence of attempts to exploit a public-facing
application. It detects attempts, not success - pair it with the web-server-spawns-shell
rule and the HTTP status code to decide whether an attempt worked.
false_positives: Vulnerability scanners run by the organisation (allow-list the scanner source IP).
Search pages or forums where users legitimately type SQL or HTML into query parameters.
query: event.dataset:zeek.http AND (url.original:(*..\/* OR *..%2f* OR *%2e%2e%2f* OR *\/etc\/passwd* OR *union%20select* OR *union\+select* OR *%3cscript* OR *\<script* OR *$\{jndi\:* OR *%24%7bjndi* OR *;\/bin\/sh* OR *%3b%2fbin%2fsh*))

name: SIGMA - SSH Session With Many Authentication Attempts
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects SSH connections in Zeek ssh.log where the server saw five or more
authentication attempts within a single connection - the pattern of password guessing
tools that reuse one TCP connection up to the server's MaxAuthTries limit. Zeek infers
attempts from the encrypted packet-size heuristics, so the count is an estimate. Tools
that open a new connection per password evade this single-event rule; the aggregation
(correlation) version is listed as future work.
false_positives: Clients that offer many keys from an SSH agent before the right one (each rejected key counts as an attempt). Set IdentitiesOnly=yes on admin hosts or raise the threshold.
query: event.dataset:zeek.ssh AND zeek.ssh.auth.attempts:>=5

name: SIGMA - Suspicious Process Access to LSASS Memory
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects a process opening a handle to lsass.exe with access rights that allow reading
its memory (PROCESS_VM_READ combined with query rights, or PROCESS_ALL_ACCESS) - the
prerequisite for credential dumping with Mimikatz, ProcDump, nanodump, etc. Known
operating-system and Defender processes that legitimately open LSASS are filtered by
full path (not by directory) so that LOLBins under System32 such as rundll32.exe are
still caught. Requires Sysmon event ID 10 with an LSASS-targeted ProcessAccess config.
false_positives: EDR / AV agents and backup software that scan LSASS. Add their exact SourceImage paths to a filter after verifying the signer.
query: (winlog.event_data.TargetImage:*\\lsass.exe AND (winlog.event_data.GrantedAccess:(0x1010 OR 0x1410 OR 0x1438 OR 0x143a OR 0x1fffff OR 0x1f1fff OR 0x1f3fff))) AND (NOT ((process.executable.caseless:(C\:\\Windows\\System32\\wininit.exe OR C\:\\Windows\\System32\\csrss.exe OR C\:\\Windows\\System32\\services.exe OR C\:\\Windows\\System32\\lsm.exe OR C\:\\Windows\\System32\\wbem\\WmiPrvSE.exe)) OR (process.executable.caseless:(C\:\\ProgramData\\Microsoft\\Windows\ Defender\\Platform\\* OR C\:\\Program\ Files\\Windows\ Defender\\*))))

name: SIGMA - Microsoft Office Application Spawning a Shell or Script Host
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan (adaptation); original SigmaHQ rule(s) by Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Markus Neis, FPT.EagleEye Team, Vadim Khrykov, Cyb3rEng, Michael Haag, Christopher Peacock @securepeacock, @scythe_io
description:
Detects a Microsoft Office application (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Publisher,
OneNote) starting a command shell, script host or a LOLBin commonly abused to fetch or
run a second stage. This is the typical process tree produced when a user opens a
weaponised attachment with a macro or an embedded object (spearphishing attachment ->
user execution). Office applications have almost no legitimate reason to start these
binaries, which makes the parent/child relationship a high-signal indicator.
false_positives: Legacy line-of-business macros that shell out (e.g. an Excel workbook that calls cmd.exe to map a drive). Baseline per host and allow-list by ParentCommandLine (document path) rather than disabling the rule.
Office add-ins that launch helper scripts during installation or updates.
query: (process.parent.executable.caseless:(*\\WINWORD.EXE OR *\\EXCEL.EXE OR *\\POWERPNT.EXE OR *\\OUTLOOK.EXE OR *\\MSPUB.EXE OR *\\ONENOTE.EXE)) AND (process.executable.caseless:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe))

name: SIGMA - PowerShell Launched With an Encoded Command
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan (adaptation); original SigmaHQ rule(s) by frack113
description:
Detects powershell.exe / pwsh.exe started with the -EncodedCommand parameter (or any of
its accepted abbreviations such as -enc, -ec, -e). The parameter takes a Base64-encoded
UTF-16LE script, which attackers use to avoid quoting problems and to hide the payload
from casual inspection of command lines. The windash modifier also matches the "/" and
Unicode-dash variants that PowerShell accepts as parameter prefixes.
false_positives: Some management agents (SCCM/ConfigMgr, Intune, Azure Guest Configuration) and installers launch encoded commands. Allow-list them by ParentImage after reviewing the decoded payload.
query: ((process.executable.caseless:(*\\powershell.exe OR *\\pwsh.exe)) OR (process.pe.original_file_name:(PowerShell.EXE OR pwsh.dll))) AND (process.command_line:(*\ \-e\ * OR *\ \/e\ * OR *\ –e\ * OR *\ —e\ * OR *\ ―e\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-ec\ * OR *\ \/ec\ * OR *\ –ec\ * OR *\ —ec\ * OR *\ ―ec\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-en\ * OR *\ \/en\ * OR *\ –en\ * OR *\ —en\ * OR *\ ―en\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-enc\ * OR *\ \/enc\ * OR *\ –enc\ * OR *\ —enc\ * OR *\ ―enc\ *) OR process.command_line:(*\ \-enco* OR *\ \/enco* OR *\ –enco* OR *\ —enco* OR *\ ―enco*))

name: SIGMA - Process Spawned by the PsExec Service (PSEXESVC)
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan (adaptation); original SigmaHQ rule(s) by Florian Roth (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects processes whose parent is PSEXESVC.exe, the service that Sysinternals PsExec
copies to the ADMIN$ share and installs on the remote host. Any child of it is a command
that was executed remotely over SMB (lateral movement) via a temporary service (service
execution). Detection happens on the *target* host, which is where the evidence is
reliable regardless of how the operator launched PsExec.
false_positives: IT administrators who legitimately use PsExec. Correlate with the source host and account in the matching 4624 logon (type 3) and allow-list admin jump hosts.
Note - does not catch Impacket psexec.py / renamed services; see docs/rules.md for the gap.
query: process.parent.executable.caseless:*\\PSEXESVC.exe

name: SIGMA - LSASS Memory Dump via comsvcs.dll MiniDump
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan (adaptation); original SigmaHQ rule(s) by Florian Roth (Nextron Systems), Modexp, Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems), Swachchhanda Shrawan Poudel (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects rundll32.exe calling the MiniDump export of comsvcs.dll (by name or by its
ordinal #24). This is a well-known "living off the land" way to write a full memory
dump of a process - in practice almost always lsass.exe - so that credentials can be
extracted offline with tools such as Mimikatz or pypykatz. It complements the
process-access rule because it fires on the command line even if Sysmon event ID 10
is not collected.
false_positives: Very unlikely. Some crash-diagnostics tooling has used this technique; confirm with the owning team before allow-listing.
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\rundll32.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:RUNDLL32.EXE) AND process.command_line:*comsvcs* AND (process.command_line:(*MiniDump* OR *#24* OR *#\+24*))

name: SIGMA - Service Created With sc.exe Pointing to a Suspicious Binary Path
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan (adaptation); original SigmaHQ rule(s) by Nasreddine Bencherchali (Nextron Systems)
description:
Detects sc.exe creating a new Windows service whose binPath points to a user-writable
directory or wraps a shell / PowerShell command. Services run as LocalSystem by default,
so creating one is both a persistence and a privilege-escalation primitive. Legitimate
installers usually register services via MSI/SCM APIs with binaries in Program Files.
false_positives: Some vendor installers and RMM tools stage service binaries in ProgramData. Verify the signer of the referenced binary and allow-list by service name.
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\sc.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:sc.exe) AND (process.command_line:*\ create\ * AND process.command_line:*binPath*) AND (process.command_line:(*\\Users\\Public\\* OR *\\AppData\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\* OR *powershell* OR *cmd\ \/c* OR *cmd.exe\ \/c* OR *%COMSPEC%*))

name: SIGMA - Scheduled Task Created With Suspicious Action or Location
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects schtasks.exe being used to create a scheduled task whose action runs a script
interpreter / LOLBin, or a binary from a user-writable directory, or downloads from a URL.
Scheduled tasks give execution, persistence (survives reboot) and, when created with
/ru SYSTEM, privilege escalation. Legitimate software normally registers tasks pointing
to binaries under Program Files, so the "suspicious action" constraint keeps volume low.
false_positives: Software updaters (browsers, chat clients) that install per-user tasks under AppData. Tune with an allow-list of known task names (/tn values) for the environment.
Administrators deploying maintenance scripts via PowerShell-based tasks.
query: (process.executable.caseless:*\\schtasks.exe OR process.pe.original_file_name:schtasks.exe) AND process.command_line:(*\ \-create\ * OR *\ \/create\ * OR *\ –create\ * OR *\ —create\ * OR *\ ―create\ *) AND (process.command_line:(*\\AppData\\* OR *\\Users\\Public\\* OR *\\Temp\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\* OR *powershell* OR *cmd\ \/c* OR *cmd.exe\ \/c* OR *mshta* OR *rundll32* OR *regsvr32* OR *wscript* OR *http\:\/\/* OR *https\:\/\/*))

name: SIGMA - Process Spawned by WinRM Remote Shell Host (wsmprovhost.exe)
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan (adaptation); original SigmaHQ rule(s) by Andreas Hunkeler (@Karneades), Markus Neis
description:
Detects child processes of wsmprovhost.exe, the host process that executes PowerShell
Remoting / WinRM sessions on the target system (Enter-PSSession, Invoke-Command). An
interactive tool or LOLBin started from it means a remote user is executing commands on
this host, which is the defining artefact of lateral movement via WinRM. conhost.exe is
filtered because it is created for every console session.
false_positives: Configuration management over WinRM (Ansible, DSC, SCCM scripts). Allow-list by the source account / management server once baselined.
query: process.parent.executable.caseless:*\\wsmprovhost.exe AND (NOT process.executable.caseless:*\\conhost.exe)

name: SIGMA - Registry Run Key Set to a Suspicious Path or Script Host
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects a value being written under the Run / RunOnce autostart keys (HKLM or HKCU,
native and WOW6432Node) whose data points to a temp / public / ProgramData location or
invokes a script host. Every program referenced there is started at user logon, which
gives persistence (and privilege escalation when an HKLM key is used). Restricting the
value data to suspicious locations removes the large volume of legitimate software that
registers itself under Program Files.
false_positives: Some installers write a RunOnce entry to a temp directory to finish setup after reboot. These are short-lived; review the binary signer.
query: (registry.path:(*\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\* OR *\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\RunOnce\\* OR *\\Software\\WOW6432Node\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run\\*)) AND (winlog.event_data.Details:(*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\* OR *\\Windows\\Temp\\* OR *\\Users\\Public\\* OR *\\ProgramData\\* OR *powershell* OR *mshta* OR *rundll32* OR *wscript* OR *cscript* OR *%TEMP%*))

name: SIGMA - UAC Bypass via Shell Open Command Hijack (ms-settings / mscfile)
author: Syed Mustafa Hassan
description:
Detects writes to HKCU\Software\Classes\ms-settings\shell\open\command or
...\mscfile\shell\open\command. Auto-elevating binaries such as fodhelper.exe,
computerdefaults.exe (ms-settings) and eventvwr.exe (mscfile) look these per-user keys
up before the machine-wide ones, so a medium-integrity user can make them start an
arbitrary command at high integrity without a UAC prompt. There is no normal reason to
create these keys in HKCU, so the rule needs no filter.
false_positives: None expected in a managed environment.
query: registry.path:(*\\Software\\Classes\\ms\-settings\\shell\\open\\command* OR *\\Software\\Classes\\mscfile\\shell\\open\\command*)
